userImpact: Whenever a job was completed in the last month, the Monthly Avg tile repeats the Lifetime Cost figure next to it; otherwise it divides by the months since the most recent job, which is not an average of anything.
evidence: monthsActive = max(1, MONTHS.between(findCompletedByUserId(userId, PageRequest.of(0,1)).first.completedDate, today)) but the query is "... completedDate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY m.completedDate DESC", so the first row is the LATEST completion. Reproduction (scratch/b1-misc.mjs), $5,636.48 over jobs on 2025-11-20, 2026-03-03, 2026-11-02, today 2026-11-09: as coded 5636.48; from the earliest completion 512.41; if the latest job were 5 months old the tile would read 1127.30. title: Searching or filtering with no matches says there are no records, notifications or events at all
userImpact: On Maintenance, searching for something that isn't there shows 'No maintenance records yet. Start tracking your home's history.' and an '+ Add First Record' button, as if the whole history were gone. On Notifications, tapping a pill such as Unread or Success when nothing matches says 'No notifications yet'. In the admin Debug event log, filtering to Errors on a healthy day says 'No events yet. Run a sync or restart', and the DB and API filter choices can never match anything, while the Home Assistant events that do exist cannot be filtered.
evidence: Rendered with 14 records, typed 'zzz' in Search: page shows "No maintenance records yet. Start tracking your home's history." and one '+ Add First Record' button. Rendered with GET /api/maintenance returning 500: same message. Code: `const data = records.data ?? [];` (L802) then `records.isLoading ? skeleton : data.length === 0 ? <first-record prompt>` (L877-889); `records.isError` is never read and the filters (server-side query params, L786-794) are not considered. Also (account-3): `{data.length === 0 ? 'No notifications yet. Activity from your home will appear here.' : 'No notifications match your filters.'}` — `data` is the server response for `params = { category, severity, unread, limit: 100 }` (lines 153-158), so any pill that matches nothing gives data.length === 0. Only the client-side search can reach the second message. `notifications.isError` is never read; on error `data = notifications.data ?? []` falls into the same branch. Also (admin-16): Empty state is shown for `!events?.length` regardless of category/level. Backend categories actually written (grep of AppEventService callers): sync, forecast, system, weather, camera, home-assistant — never db, api or auth. Runtime: Category=DB with 4 events in the log -> "No events yet. Run a sync or restart to populate."
fix: Show a 'nothing matches' message whenever a filter or search is active, with a Clear filters button. Maintenance (L877-889): if `filters.category || filters.status || filters.priority || debouncedSearch` show 'No records match these filters' + Clear filters; keep the first-record prompt only for a successful, unfiltered, empty result. Notifications: `const filtering = !!(categoryFilter || severityFilter || unreadOnly || deferredSearch.trim())` picks the message (L303). Debug (DebugDashboard.tsx:788): when category or level is not 'all' show 'No events match these filters'; remove the DB and API options and add { key: 'home-assistant', label: 'Home Assistant' } to CATEGORIES (L113-114). The failed-load half of these screens is covered by the 'When data fails to load' entry.

title: When data fails to load, many screens say 'nothing here yet' (or show $0.00 / 0 kWh) instead of saying the load failed
area: Several screens > loading and error states
userImpact: During a server restart, a deploy or a weak connection, screens tell the family something untrue and offer no Retry. Water says no bills have ever synced and points at the Gmail sync. Electric and Gas say 'No CoServ bills synced yet'. Maintenance offers '+ Add First Record' and shows $0.00 costs. Roomba says it has never cleaned and has no map. Users says 'No users found', Notifications 'No notifications yet', Guests '0 active'. The NUC, thermostat and camera-battery charts say 'Nothing to draw yet' or 'Collecting data'. The Electric tiles read 0 kWh and $0.00. Home's Maintenance card sits on 'Loading...' forever, Home's weather card silently disappears, and Debug tabs go blank. This only happens when the first load fails (a failed background refresh keeps the last good data), but then the message is actively wrong.
evidence: Each screen branches on isLoading and then on 'no data', never on isError. A React Query whose first load fails ends as {isLoading:false, isError:true, data:undefined} and so falls into the empty branch (reproduced with the app's @tanstack/query-core 5.101.4). Rendered against the built app with mocked failures: Maintenance -> 'No maintenance records yet' + tiles '$0.00'; Guests -> '0' + 'No guest sessions found'; NUC history -> 4 x 'Nothing to draw yet'; Electric -> '60-Day Total 0 kWh', '60-DAY SPEND $0.00', 'ACTIVE READINGS 0'; Debug Forecast tab -> nothing under the tab bar. Code: WaterUsage.tsx:158 `{!hasData && !loading ? <EmptyChart ... 'No water bills synced yet...'`; GasUsage.tsx:188 `if (!loading && !latest)`; CoservBillingHistory.tsx:39 `{!hasData && !loading && ...}`; HomeSummary.tsx:137 `m ? ... : 'Loading...'`; HomeSummary.tsx:222 `... : currentWx ? <section/> : null`; Roomba.tsx:775 `runs.length === 0 ? 'No cleaning runs yet'`; UserManagement.tsx:205; Notifications.tsx:295-306; combineHistory (Climate.tsx:58) and combineBattery (Cameras.tsx:104) drop isError; MaintenanceDashboard.tsx:135 `formatCurrency(a?.totalLifetimeCost ?? 0)`. api/client.ts only console.errors and queryClient.ts has no global onError, so nothing else surfaces the failure. The app already does it right in Cameras.tsx:149, Climate.tsx:102, NucHealth.tsx:521, TabUsage.tsx:97, Updates.tsx:65-75 and the Roomba status strip (Roomba.tsx:496).
fix: Add one small shared component, e.g. components/LoadError.tsx ("Couldn't load {what}." + errorMessage(error) + a Retry button calling refetch()). At each listed place insert `query.isError && !query.data ? <LoadError .../> :` ahead of the empty-state branch; keep the `&& !query.data` guard so a failed background refresh keeps showing the last good data. Where a number is shown, render '—' instead of defaulting to 0 when there is no data (Maintenance SummaryCards L135-137, Electric tiles and header L392-413, Guests 'Active Guests'). Specifics: HomeSummary.tsx:137 use maintenance.isLoading for 'Loading...'; HomeSummary.tsx:222 render a one-line 'Weather is unavailable right now' card instead of null; Home tiles (L236-283) show a pulse placeholder while loading; pass `errored` through combineHistory and combineBattery to the two charts; give RoombaMap an `error` prop; in DebugDashboard read isLoading/isError for diagnostics, summary, freshness, configCheck, syncHistory and coverage. Start with Water, Gas and the shared Billing History, which name a wrong cause.

title: Tapping many text boxes and dropdowns on an iPhone probably zooms the whole app in, because their text is 15px (iOS zooms anything under 16px)
area: Several screens > text boxes on iPhone
userImpact: If iOS behaves as it normally does, focusing one of these controls zooms the app in and leaves it zoomed, pushing dialog buttons off-screen until the person pinches back out. Affected: the Roomba clean and rename dialogs, the Maintenance form and search box, the Weather alert time fields, the Notifications search and the admin pages. The sign-in, Register, Edit Profile and guest sign-in boxes are already 16px and unaffected.
evidence: Below 1024px, `--text-sm: 0.9375rem` (index.css:90) makes every text-sm control 15px; Chromium computed style at 390px for the CleanModal select is font-size 15px, and the Maintenance 'Or custom...' and Search boxes are 13px (text-xs). A scan of src found 41 of 55 text-entry controls at text-sm or smaller. The viewport meta (index.html:6) is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover` with no maximum-scale, and index.css has no rule lifting form controls to 16px. Editor's spot-check: Login.tsx's inputs carry no text-sm and inherit 16px, so the remark in maintenance-wifi-guest-17 that the sign-in page has the same small boxes is wrong. The zoom itself is iOS behaviour that could not be run here (no WebKit build; desktop WebKit doesn't emulate it).
fix: First confirm on an iPhone: open Roomba > Clean and tap the first dropdown, or tap the Maintenance Search box, and see whether the page zooms. If it does, add one base rule to index.css after the Tailwind import, in an unlayered block so it beats the text-sm utility: `@media (max-width: 1023px) { input:not([type='checkbox']):not([type='radio']):not([type='range']), select, textarea { font-size: 1rem; } }`. Don't use maximum-scale=1 in the viewport meta (it would also block pinch-zoom). Check the pill-shaped filter controls still fit afterwards.

title: Opening the app during a brief server or network hiccup throws a signed-in person out to the sign-in page (or nginx's bare 502 page)
userImpact: If the session check fails for any reason other than a rejected token (a 502 while the backend restarts, weak Wi-Fi, Tailscale still connecting, a 30 s timeout), the person lands on 'Welcome Back'; on the secure address the page then jumps to /api/auth/oidc/start, which during an outage is nginx's bare 502 page.
evidence: AuthContext.tsx:110-121: for a non-401/403 error it does `setUser(null); return;` (token kept) and `.finally(() => setIsLoading(false))`; nothing retries. Guard.tsx:19: `if (!token || !user) return <Navigate to="/login" .../>`. Login.tsx:62-65: a failed `oidcConfig()` falls back to `{ sso: isHttps, password: false }`, and the effect at 71-75 then calls `startHomeSso()` = `window.location.assign('/api/auth/oidc/start')`. nginx/default.conf has no `error_page` for /api/. The existing test is even named 'should redirect to /login when token validation fails' and feeds it `new Error('no backend')`.
fix: Add a third state to AuthContext, e.g. `sessionCheck: 'ok' | 'checking' | 'unreachable'`. On a non-auth failure set 'unreachable', keep the token, and retry `fetchMe` with backoff and on `visibilitychange`/`online`. In ProtectedRoute, when a token exists and the state is 'unreachable', render a 'Can't reach home right now - Retry' card instead of `<Navigate to="/login">`. Update Guards.test.tsx:58 to assert that card for a network error and the redirect only for 401/403.

title: In the light theme, card shadows stop in a hard straight line under some sections (and edge focus outlines are cut off)

evidence: Rendered in Chromium with the app's built CSS (scratch/b3-browser.cjs, screenshots b3-shadow-perf-chromium-light.png vs b3-shadow-plain-chromium-light.png): the same two cards inside `perf-section grid` have the shadow clipped to the grid box (visible only in the gap and as wedges under the rounded corners), while without `perf-section` the shadow fades out normally. b3-modules-focus-chromium-light.png shows the focused module link's outline cut off on its left, top and bottom. title: Pop-up windows don't take keyboard focus, and on an iPhone a back-swipe leaves the page instead of closing several of them
userImpact: With a keyboard or VoiceOver, opening a pop-up leaves focus on the page behind it. This covers What's New, a bill, the 24-hour forecast, the Roomba run details and clean/rename/divide/merge windows, Edit Profile, the Maintenance details and Add/Edit forms, the enlarged Wi-Fi QR code, a camera recording and the Debug event details. Tab walks the hidden page, and closing the pop-up doesn't return focus to the button that opened it. On an iPhone, swiping back with a Roomba run, the forecast or the Maintenance form open leaves the page instead of closing the pop-up. Edit Profile and the Maintenance forms aren't marked as pop-ups at all, so dragging down inside them triggers the app's pull-to-refresh behind them. The Wi-Fi QR pop-up also ignores Escape (every other pop-up honours it), and the Debug event close button is read out as an unnamed '✕'. Touch use otherwise works: every pop-up closes with its button or a tap outside.
evidence: Repo-wide, useFocusTrap( is called only in App.tsx:154 (phone menu), ConfirmThermostatChangeModal.tsx:28 and DebugDashboard.tsx:1180, and useBackToClose( only in BillPdfModal.tsx:84 and CameraRecordings.tsx:88. The other overlays use useScrollLock plus a hand-rolled Escape listener; ReleaseNotesModal.tsx creates a panelRef and never reads it. Rendered Add Maintenance: overlay role=null, aria-modal=null, activeElement stays on '+ Add Maintenance', four Tabs land on 'Cards', 'Timeline', 'All Categories', 'All Statuses'. A 300px touch-drag from the top of the open form armed the pull-to-refresh chip and fired a GET /api/maintenance, because PullToRefresh.tsx:19 only skips [role="dialog"], [data-no-pull] (UserEditModal.tsx:68 has the same gap). WiFiPage.tsx:167-172 has no keydown handler and its opener (L92) only handles Enter. DebugDashboard.tsx:1215 close button has no aria-label and focus lands on BODY after Escape: these modals are unmounted rather than switched to open=false, so the trap's return-focus effect never runs (same reason ConfirmThermostatChangeModal loses focus).
fix: Make one shared Dialog wrapper (e.g. components/Dialog.tsx) and move these overlays onto it: role='dialog' + aria-modal + aria-labelledby on the panel (not the backdrop), useFocusTrap(open, panelRef, undefined, onClose) (it already handles Escape, so delete the hand-rolled key listeners), useBackToClose(onClose), useScrollLock, and restore focus on unmount by saving document.activeElement on mount and focusing it in the cleanup (needed because these are unmounted, not toggled). Also: aria-label='Close' on DebugDashboard.tsx:1215; turn the Wi-Fi QR opener (WiFiPage.tsx:92) into a real <button>; let RoomRenameModal's input keep first focus. The same wrapper is the natural place for the opaque panel background (see the see-through pop-ups entry).

title: On phones the Cameras header art cuts off the top of the solar camera
userImpact: The solar panel on top of the pixel-art camera post is sliced off (top 9px, 3 of its 5 panel rows) in the phone header strip.
evidence: Reproduction (scratch/b2.js parsing the sprite grids): `SOLOCAM: rows=17 compact needs 57px of 48 (clip 9px)`. compactSpec sets `scale: Math.max(2, (item.scale ?? 4) - 1)` = 3; 17 rows x 3 + GROUND_H 6 = 57px in an `h-12` (48px) strip whose wrapper in PageHeader is `w-full overflow-hidden lg:hidden`. fix: In compactSpec clamp the scale to the strip: `scale: Math.min(Math.max(2, (item.scale ?? 4) - 1), Math.floor((48 - GROUND_H) / item.art.grid.length))` (gives 2 for SOLOCAM, unchanged for the rest). Alternatively make the compact strip `h-[3.75rem]`.

title: With the Light theme chosen, the app opens dark navy and then flips to light
userImpact: Every cold start or auto-reload with Light (or Auto in daytime, or a light-mode phone) shows a dark screen until the JavaScript has loaded, then one frame of the app in dark colours, then light.
evidence: Measured in Chromium against the existing build served from a scratch script, with localStorage theme='light' and the JS delayed 300 ms (scratch/b3-flash.cjs). Per-frame [ms, data-theme, body background, React mounted]: [51, null, rgb(2, 6, 23), false] -> [321, null, rgb(2, 6, 23), true] -> [336, 'light', rgb(238, 241, 246), true]; first-paint was at 64 ms. index.html has no inline script, `:root` is the dark theme, and `data-theme` is only set in a `useEffect`.
fix: Add a tiny inline script at the top of index.html <head> that sets `data-theme` and `data-palette` before first paint: read localStorage 'theme' ('light'/'dark' used directly; otherwise `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)')`) and 'palette'. For Auto, have ThemeProvider also store the last resolved theme (e.g. 'theme-resolved') and let the script use it. Change the two attribute effects (lines 268 and 310) to `useLayoutEffect` to remove the one dark frame after mount. No CSP is set in nginx or the backend, so an inline script is allowed.

title: Once a theme is picked there is no way to go back to following the phone's light/dark setting
userImpact: Tapping the menu's light/dark switch once, or any Theme option, permanently stops the app following the device's light/dark setting; only clearing site data brings it back.
evidence: MODES lists only light, dark and auto; `setMode` is called only from ThemePicker.tsx:42 with those values and from `toggleTheme` (`setMode(theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')`). 'system' is reachable only as `readStoredMode()`'s fallback when nothing is stored (`if (mode === 'system') localStorage.removeItem('theme')`), and the 'Following your device setting.' helper text shows only in that state.
fix: In ThemePicker.tsx add a fourth option `{ mode: 'system', label: '📱 Device' }` and change the active test to `mode === m` (dropping the 'system highlights the resolved theme' special case); check the four pills still fit a phone row (the group already has flex-wrap).

title: After signing in again you always land on Home, not the page (or alert) you were trying to open
userImpact: Tap a phone alert for Cameras or Notifications after the session has lapsed (it lasts 24 hours) and you end up on the Home dashboard and have to find the page again.
evidence: Guard.tsx:20 `<Navigate to="/login" state={{ from: location }} replace />` and AuthContext.tsx:77-79 says the redirect is 'remembering where the user was', but Login.tsx never calls useLocation or reads state: both exits are `navigate('/', { replace: true })` (lines 85 and 119). Grep for `location.state` / `state?.from` across src finds no reader. Push taps deep-link via sw.js:31 (`data.url`), and JWTs expire after 24 h with no refresh (application.yml:39).
fix: Login.tsx: (1) password path, read `(useLocation().state as { from?: Location })?.from` and navigate to `from.pathname + from.search` instead of '/'; (2) SSO path, the full-page redirect drops router state, so before `startHomeSso()` (line 74) and on the 'Sign in with Home' link click store that path in sessionStorage, then after `oidcExchange()` (line 85) navigate to it and remove the key. Only accept same-origin paths starting with '/'.

title: The Create Account page still shows its full form when password sign-in is turned off, then rejects it on submit
userImpact: Someone who opens /register from an old link fills in five fields and only then learns that accounts are no longer created this way.
evidence: Register.tsx never calls `oidcConfig()` and renders the form unconditionally; the route is public and unconditional (main.tsx:107). Server: `if (!passwordLoginEnabled) return ResponseEntity.status(403).body(PASSWORD_LOGIN_OFF);` (AuthController:37) and production defaults to off (`PASSWORD_LOGIN_ENABLED: ${PASSWORD_LOGIN_ENABLED:-false}`, docker-compose.yml:80). Login.tsx hides only the link (`{options?.password && ... <Link to="/register">`).
fix: In Register.tsx load `oidcConfig()` on mount (same call Login.tsx:62 makes); while `passwordLogin` is false render a short card ('Accounts are added by the admin. Use Sign in with Home.') with a link to /login instead of the form.

title: A cancelled or unfinished Roomba run is described as "Last cleaned" on Home
userImpact: Start a clean and cancel it two minutes later, and Home says "Last cleaned Nov 9 · 14 sq ft" as if the house had been cleaned today.
evidence: Line 159: `${lastRun?.status === 'STUCK' ? 'Last run got stuck' : 'Last cleaned'} ...` with `fetchRoombaRuns(1)` (newest run of any status). The poller writes CANCELLED and INCOMPLETE runs with a completed_at (poller.py:766-773, 812). Reproduction: status 'CANCELLED', 14 sq ft -> 'Last cleaned Nov 9 · 14 sq ft'.
fix: In roombaDetail (line 159) branch on status: STUCK -> 'Last run got stuck', CANCELLED -> 'Last run cancelled', anything other than COMPLETED -> 'Last run ended early', COMPLETED -> 'Last cleaned'. (Alternative: fetch a few runs and show the newest COMPLETED one.)

title: Home keeps showing the Roomba's last known state as live when the robot data has gone stale
userImpact: If the Roomba poller stops while the last snapshot said it was running, Home goes on saying "Cleaning 64% · Cleaning now" indefinitely, with no hint the reading is old.
evidence: HomeSummary never reads `rb.online` or `rb.updatedAt` (lines 103-162, 259-265). The backend computes `online` = snapshot within 10 min (RoombaService.java:58, 698) and the Roomba tab uses it: `{status?.online ? 'Online' : status ? 'Offline' : 'No data'}` + 'updated N min ago' (Roomba.tsx:443-446). Reproduction: online:false + phase 'run' -> 'Cleaning 64%' / 'Cleaning now · 312 sq ft'.

title: Weather shows a sun icon after dark on winter evenings (and before dawn), because 'night' is a fixed 8 PM to 6 AM
userImpact: In November-January a clear evening shows a sun from sunset (about 5:30 PM) until 8 PM, while the app's own Auto theme has already gone dark.
evidence: Ran the app's sun.ts algorithm against the fixed rule for North Texas (scratch/b10/sun.mjs): `Nov 9 sunrise 6:53 AM sunset 5:30 PM | mismatched hours: 6:30 dark but day icon, 18:30 dark but day icon, 19:30 dark but day icon`; `Dec 21 sunset 5:25 PM | 6:30, 17:30, 18:30, 19:30 dark but day icon`; `Jun 21 sunset 8:40 PM | 20:30 light but night icon`. Code: l.38-41 `const hour = new Date().getHours(); return hour >= 20 || hour < 6;` and l.59 the same test per forecast hour.
fix: weather.ts — give isNightTime/getWeatherEmoji/getWeatherEmojiForHour an optional location and decide with `isDaytime(date, lat, lon)` from utils/sun.ts, falling back to the current 20/6 rule when it returns null. The coordinates are already available client-side (ThemeContext stores them under localStorage 'sun-location' from /api/config); for forecast hours build the Date from the hour's `time` string so each column uses that day's sunrise/sunset. Update frontend/src/test/weather.test.ts accordingly.

title: When the phone is in another time zone, the forecast's 'Now' tile is the wrong hour for home
userImpact: Checking the house from the West Coast, the tile labelled 'Now' is home's weather from two hours ago; from the East Coast the current hour is skipped.
evidence: Reproduced (scratch/b3-tz.cjs) at 12:00 home time: device in America/Chicago -> strip starts 12:00; America/Los_Angeles -> key '...T10:00', strip starts at home's 10:00 labelled 'Now'; America/New_York -> starts at 13:00. The key is built from device-local `getHours()` and string-compared with Open-Meteo hours the backend requests with `&timezone=America/Chicago`.
fix: Build the key in the home's zone in `nowLocalKey()`: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'America/Chicago', year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit', hour: '2-digit', hourCycle: 'h23' }).formatToParts(new Date())` and assemble 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00'. Do the same for 'today' in `dayLabel()` (line 35) so 'Today/Tomorrow' follow home too.

title: Screen readers announce the Electric / Gas / Water and sub-tab switchers as tabs, but they have no linked panels and arrow keys do nothing
userImpact: A screen reader announces 'tab, 1 of 3' but there is no associated panel and the Left/Right keys a tab list promises do nothing; the content below is not announced as belonging to the selected tab.
evidence: `role="tablist"` + `role="tab" aria-selected={active}` buttons with no `id`/`aria-controls`, no `tabIndex` management or key handler; the content is rendered in a bare `<Suspense>` with no `role="tabpanel"`. Grep for `role="tabpanel"` in frontend/src returns nothing.

A small shared `<Tabs>` component would cover Utility, ElectricalUsage and Roomba (and the similar lists in Cameras, DebugDashboard, TabUsage).

title: Utility forgets which view (Gas/Water) and which Electric sub-tab you were on after a reload, Back, or the app's sleep screen
userImpact: After choosing Water, a reload, an app-update reload, coming Back from another page, or waking the sleep screen lands on Electric again; arriving from Home's water link and switching to Electric snaps back to Water the same way.
evidence: `const [params] = useSearchParams(); const [view, setView] = useState<UtilityView>(viewFromParam(params.get('view')));` and `onClick={() => setView(tab.key)}`: the URL is read once at mount and never written. App.tsx:495 unmounts the page while asleep (`{!asleep && (<ErrorBoundary key={pathname}><Outlet /></ErrorBoundary>)}`). ElectricalUsage.tsx:45 `useState<ElectricTab>('usage')` has the same shape. DebugDashboard.tsx:237-248 already drives its tab from the query string, and App.tsx:109 says scroll is 'Keyed on pathname only, so sub-tab (?view=) changes keep their scroll', i.e. the shell expects ?view= to change.
fix: Utility.tsx: `const [params, setParams] = useSearchParams(); const view = viewFromParam(params.get('view'));` and on click `setParams((prev) => { const next = new URLSearchParams(prev); if (key === 'electric') next.delete('view'); else next.set('view', key); return next; }, { replace: true })` (the DebugDashboard pattern). Do the same for the Electric sub-tab with a `tab` param.

title: The 7-Day and 30-Day electric averages quietly drop their oldest day every evening (6 PM in winter, 7 PM in summer)
userImpact: The "7-Day Avg" tile averages 6 days and the "30-Day Avg" 29 days when viewed in the evening, so the figures differ from the morning with no new data.
evidence: Function re-run in node with TZ=America/Chicago (scratch/b10/logic.mjs): `Nov 9 17:59 CST | 7d thr 2026-11-02 days 7 avg 35.00 | 30d thr 2026-10-10 days 30 avg 45.97` then `Nov 9 18:00 CST | 7d thr 2026-11-03 days 6 avg 36.50 | 30d thr 2026-10-11 days 29 avg 46.17`; in summer the flip is at 19:00 CDT (`2026-07-15T18:59 thr 2026-07-08`, `19:00 thr 2026-07-09`). Cause: l.184-186 `new Date(now.getTime() - days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` is a UTC date compared with local-calendar `p.date`.
fix: usageSummary.ts:184-186 — build the cutoff from local calendar fields with the helper already in the file: `const t = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate() - days); const threshold = formatDateOnly(t);`. Add a test in frontend/src/test/usageSummary.test.ts with `now` set to an evening Central time (the existing tests all use 12:00Z, which hides this).

title: 'Forecast Accuracy Over Time' chart has two lines and no legend
userImpact: People can't tell which line is the daily miss and which is the 7-day average.
evidence: screenshot utility-electric-forecast-desktop-dark-full.png: orange dotted line + green smooth line, no key; the forecast chart directly above has a legend (ForecastChart.tsx:429-447). Code: <ComposedChart data={dailyAccData}> with <Line dataKey="error"> and <Line dataKey="trailing"> and no legend row.

title: Forecast accuracy card says "no data" while it is still loading, and the hourly message always says "past week"
userImpact: Switching to Hourly, or to a different range, briefly shows "No hourly readings to grade in the past week yet" / "Not enough graded predictions in this range yet" before the chart appears, and the hourly wording is wrong when 2 Weeks or 1 Month is selected.
evidence: `const { data: rangeAccuracy } = useQuery(...)` / `const { data: hourlyAccuracy } = useQuery({... enabled: accGranularity === 'hourly' })` - isLoading is never read; `dailyAccData`/`hourlyAccData` fall back to `[]`, so `length < 2` renders the empty box. Query keys include the range and no placeholderData is set (queryClient.ts defaults: staleTime, retry, refetchOnWindowFocus only), so each new range starts with data undefined. Hourly ranges are 7d/14d/30d (lines 54-55, 581) but the copy is fixed to "past week"; the JSX comment on line 560 ("hourly is fixed to a week") is stale.

Optionally add `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` so switching ranges keeps the old chart until the new one arrives.

title: Forecast chart tooltip shows code names ("confidenceBand", "predicted", "actual") and no kWh
userImpact: Tapping or hovering a day on the forecast chart shows lines like "confidenceBand : 22.59 ~ 29.39" and "predicted : 25.99" instead of plain labels with units.

Installed recharts 2.15.4: ChartUtils.js:1071 `name: name || dataKey`, DefaultTooltipContent.js:29 `value.join(' ~ ')`, unit printed from `entry.unit || ''`. The two accuracy charts in the same file (lines 626-632, 681-691) do pass a formatter.

title: The 'Today' marker label sits on top of the chart lines
userImpact: 'Today' is drawn across the dashed marker and the actual/predicted lines, so it reads as 'To|day' and hides part of the data.

title: Home and the Electric tab can name different days as the latest electric reading while yesterday is still posting
userImpact: On a morning when CoServ has only part of yesterday posted, the Last Reading tile shows the day before while the Usage Log right under it and the Home tile both show yesterday's part-day total.
evidence: Three different 'complete day' rules: ElectricalUsage.tsx:110 `>= 20` non-zero hourly rows (comment on 107 says 24); :263 `>= 18` non-zero rows; HomeSummary.tsx:37 and usageSummary.ts:188 `readingCount >= 18`, where readingCount is the server's COUNT(*) including 0.00 rows. Reproduced in the built app (frontend/dist, mocked API, yesterday = 24 rows / 19 non-zero / 28.5 kWh, earlier days 48 kWh): Last Reading tile 'Last Reading 48.0 kWh Nov 7'; Usage Log first row 'Nov 8 28.50'; Home 'LAST DAILY ELECTRIC 28.5kWh Sun, Nov 8'; 7-Day Avg 45.2 (part-day included). Also (consistency-25): Home line 37: `.filter((d) => d.readingCount >= 18)` on the server's COUNT(*) of hourly rows (EnergyUsageService.java:59, zero-kWh rows included). ElectricalUsage.tsx:110: `>= 20` on client-counted rows with usage > 0 (realData filter, lines 59-66), falling back to the newest partial day; the log at 263 uses `>= 18`; the comment at 107 says '24 complete hourly records'. Reproduction (scratch/b5.js) with yesterday at 19 rows: Home tile 2026-11-08 22.4 | Electric Last Reading 2026-11-07 31.2 | Electric log rows 2026-11-08, 2026-11-07. Editor's note: consistency-25 doubted the 18-19-hour window occurs, but tooling-4 reproduced the disagreement in the built bundle and also covers days with 18+ rows of which some are 0.00 placeholders — a state HourlySyncScheduler's own comment documents ('a 24-row-but-mostly-zero day').
fix: Use one rule everywhere. Replace the literal 20 (ElectricalUsage.tsx:110) and the literals 18 (ElectricalUsage.tsx:263, HomeSummary.tsx:37) with COMPLETE_DAY_MIN_HOURS and correct the '24 complete hourly records' comment. To make Home and the averages agree with the Electric tab, have the /daily endpoint count real readings (COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE usage_kwh > 0) in EnergyUsageService.getDailyAggregates) so readingCount means the same thing as the client-side count.

title: The explanation of how the Predicted Bill was worked out only appears on mouse hover, so it can't be seen on a phone
userImpact: On the iPhone Home Screen app there is no way to see what the predicted bill is made of (metered kWh, forecast kWh, fixed charge and rate, 'gas is billed separately'); keyboard users can't reach it either.
evidence: `title={billProjection ? describeBillProjection(billProjection) : undefined}` is passed to StatTile, which only sets `<div title={title} ...>` on a non-focusable div (StatTile.tsx:47-49). iOS Safari never shows title tooltips and there is no tap or focus alternative.
fix: Give StatTile an optional `info` text: render a small 'i' button in the tile header with aria-expanded that toggles the paragraph inline under the subtitle (or in the existing modal-panel pattern on phones). Pass describeBillProjection() to it from ElectricalUsage.tsx:378 and keep `title` as the desktop extra.

title: Low and High tiles keep showing a loading '...' when a period has no readings
userImpact: On the 1st of a month (and whenever the summaries request fails) the Current Month card shows '...' for Low and High as if still loading, above 'No data', next to '0 readings' and '0.0 kWh'.
evidence: `{loading || !summary.lowest ? '...' : `${summary.lowest.usageKwh.toFixed(1)} ${unitLabel}`}`; `createEmptyUsageSummary` returns `highest: null, lowest: null`; backend EnergyUsageService.getSummaryViaJpa returns `.orElse(null)` for both when the range has no rows; ElectricalUsage.tsx:238 also substitutes the empty summary when `batchSummary.data` is undefined (request failed) while `summaryLoading` is false.

title: A gas rate that ends in zero would lose it on the last-bill breakdown ('9 CCF × $1.3')

title: Gas 'Next bill' switches to 'Any day' at 6 PM on the expected bill date instead of the day after

In July the flip happens at 19:01.

title: When a bill fails to load, the dialog says to try "Open raw PDF", but that link does nothing
userImpact: On a network error, a missing file, or for a Guest-role account (always refused with 403), the dialog points to a link that looks normal but has no destination; the same link is silently inert while the bill is still loading.

Try "Open raw PDF" above. - while the link is <a href={rawUrl ?? undefined} aria-disabled={!rawUrl}> with no disabled styling. errorMessage() on an arraybuffer 403/404 returns the fallback, so the text reads "(couldn't load the bill)". BillFileController returns 403 unless role is ADMIN or USER.

title: Water bill discounts are shown as '$-1.50' instead of '-$1.50'

Screenshot review: screenshot utility-water-phone-dark-full.png: 'DISCOUNT $-1.50' appears on every bill. Code: `const money = (n?: number) => (n == null ? '—' : `$${n.toFixed(2)}`);` (line 59) is used for `bill.achDiscount` (line 264).

title: Thermostat history charts show odd, unevenly spaced temperature marks (78°, 71.7°, 67.7°, 63.7°), on different scales per room

Screenshot review: screenshot climate-phone-dark-full.png: the Downstairs axis reads 78°, 71.7°, 67.7°, 63.7° with a larger gap at the top; Upstairs reads 72°, 66.3°, 63.3°. Code: `domain={['dataMin - 2', 'dataMax + 2']}` with `allowDecimals={false}` (lines 159-160). The fractional readings become fractional domain ends, and those ends are printed as ticks.

title: Time axes on battery and thermostat charts skip hours irregularly (5 PM, 6 PM, 8 PM, 10 PM, 11 PM...)

Code: <XAxis dataKey="t" type="number" scale="time" domain={domain} tickFormatter={(t) => formatTick(t, range)} minTickGap=...> with no explicit ticks; formatTick shows the hour only (same in ThermostatHistoryChart.tsx:142-152).

title: 'Can't reach Home Assistant' banner shows when it's actually the server or Wi-Fi that's down
userImpact: During a NUC deploy or a Wi-Fi drop, the banner blames Home Assistant, pointing whoever reads it at the wrong thing.
evidence: Banner renders for any `thermostatsQuery.isError` with data; HomeDeviceService: '// thermostat reads (served from Postgres; 503 only when the integration is off)' (CameraService.listCameras is the same), so a failed refresh is never caused by HA being down.
fix: Pick the copy by errorStatus: 503 -> current Home Assistant text; null (network) -> "Can't reach the server — showing data from …"; otherwise errorMessage(error). Apply the same to Cameras.tsx:204.

title: A 'Can't go higher/lower' hint stays under the thermostat and hides 'Set by …' until the next change
userImpact: After a blocked tap, the hint replaces the 'Set by Mai · 4:56 PM' line for as long as the page stays open, even after a mode change or someone else's change.
evidence: useEffect(() => { if (!cmd.draft) setHint(null); }, [cmd.draft]); the blocked branch does `setHint(...); return;` without queueing a draft, so draft stays null and the effect never re-runs; status chain has `else if (hint)` ahead of `cmd.notice` and `attributionText(...)`.
fix: Give blocked hints a lifetime: in stepRange's blocked branch start a ~4 s timer (ref, cleared on unmount and on the next step) that calls setHint(null); or keep them in a separate `blockedHint` state reset when t.lastChange?.at or t.hvacMode changes.

title: At a temperature limit, the hint blames the other tile ('Can't go higher, cool-to…' when lowering Heat to)
userImpact: With Heat to at 45° tapping − says "Can't go higher — cool-to is at the 92° limit", and with Cool to at 92° tapping + says "Can't go lower — heat-to is at the 45° limit": the wrong side and direction.
evidence: node scratch/b11/range.cjs (normalizeRange copied verbatim): 'Heat to at 45, tap − -> Can't go higher — cool-to is at the 92° limit.' / 'Cool to at 92, tap + -> Can't go lower — heat-to is at the 45° limit.' normalizeRange returns blocked when the tapped side itself can't move (`nextLow === low` -> blocked: delta !== 0).
fix: In stepRange pick the copy from field + delta: low with delta<0 -> `Heat to can't go below ${lim.min}°.`; high with delta>0 -> `Cool to can't go above ${lim.max}°.`; keep the current text only for the push-blocked cases (low +1, high -1). Also pass lowerDisabled={shownLow != null && shownLow <= lim.min} and raiseDisabled={shownHigh != null && shownHigh >= lim.max} to the range tiles, as the single tile already does.

title: Empty 'Comfort' heading can show during a hold if the thermostat offers no presets
userImpact: A thermostat on hold that reports no selectable presets would show a lone 'COMFORT' label with nothing under it.
evidence: `{canControl && (presets.length > 0 || isHold(t.presetMode)) && (… {presets.map(…)} …)}` with selectablePresets dropping 'temp'; Resume lives in the separate hold row.
fix: Render the Comfort block only when `presets.length > 0`.

title: Tapping a mode right after ± still sends the old temperature a second later
userImpact: If someone taps + and then another mode within 1.2 s, the queued temperature goes out after the mode change: it can land on the new mode's setpoint, or fail with an error ('Mode heat_cool needs low and high', 'Thermostat is off'), or end in 'ecobee hasn't confirmed yet'.
evidence: changeMode: `setError(null); setNotice(null); setPendingMode(m); mode.mutate(m);` leaves sendTimer/queued alone; ThermostatCard `disabled = !t.available || cmd.busy` and busy only covers in-flight mutations, so the mode buttons work during 'Sending in a moment…'. Backend setTemperature checks the single/range shape against the stored mode.
fix: At the top of changeMode (and the hold/resume wrappers) cancel the batch: `if (sendTimer.current) clearTimeout(sendTimer.current); queued.current = null; setDraft(null); setDraftSentAt(null);`. Or flush it first (temperature.mutate(queued) then the mode).

title: Thermostat mode buttons read the current mode as 'dimmed' and don't respond to arrow keys
userImpact: VoiceOver announces the selected mode as 'Heat, selected, dimmed', and keyboard users get four Tab stops with no arrow-key movement in what's announced as a radio group.
evidence: `role="radiogroup"` with buttons `role="radio" aria-checked={active} aria-disabled={active || disabled}`; no roving tabIndex or ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handler.
fix: Set aria-disabled only from `disabled` (the onClick already ignores the active option); add roving tabIndex (checked = 0, others = -1) and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End handlers. Or drop the radio roles and use buttons with aria-pressed. The Comfort pills (line 347) use the same aria-disabled-on-active pattern.

title: Any battery charging is shown as sun (☀️ / '+X% sun'), even a USB top-up
userImpact: A camera charged from a cable would show '☀️ Charging' and its day chip would read '+20% sun' for a night with no sun.
evidence: BatteryBadge `{state === 'charging' ? '☀️ ' : ''}{label}` while chargeLabel returns plain 'Charging' when chargingStatus isn't solar; the chip prints `+{d.gained}% sun` for every rise. CameraLinker documents eufy labels 'Solar charging', 'Charging', 'Plugged'…
fix: Show ☀️ only when /solar/i.test(camera.chargingStatus) (or the rise falls in a daylight window); word the chip '+X% charged' unless the gain is solar or in daylight.

title: Dark mode: the Cameras 'Live / Recordings' switch doesn't show which side is selected
userImpact: The selected half has the same fill as the track, so only a slightly brighter word marks the current view. The switch is also styled differently from every other tab switch in the app, which use a green tint.
evidence: screenshot cameras-live-phone-dark.png: the selected 'Live' fill is #0e1629 and the track is #101925, about 1.0:1. Code: `view === v ? 'bg-appsurface-raised text-apptext shadow-sm' : 'text-apptext-muted hover:text-apptext'` (line 35).
fix: Use the shared active style `bg-appaccent-soft text-appaccent-text` (as in ElectricalUsage.tsx:434 and Roomba.tsx:527).

title: '● LIVE' and the live controls stay on a frozen picture for 2 s before reconnecting
userImpact: When a stream drops, the tile keeps LIVE, the pan/tilt arrows, full screen and Stop over a frozen frame for 2 more seconds (8 s in all after an HLS stall) before 'Connecting…'.
evidence: onEnded only schedules `window.setTimeout(() => setSession((s) => s + 1), 2_000)`; status stays 'playing' so `live = streaming && status === 'playing'` stays true until the remounted LiveVideo reports 'connecting'. HLS_STALL_MS = 6_000 triggers onEnded after 6 s frozen.
fix: Call `setStatus('connecting')` at the start of onEnded's reconnect branch.

title: A live-view error stays on a camera tile after you leave the app and come back
userImpact: After locking the phone and reopening the Home Screen app on Cameras, a tile that showed 'Live view keeps dropping' earlier still shows it and needs Try again, while the other tiles go live.
evidence: Comment: 'Leaving the tab ends the visit: coming back starts live again…'; effect: `if (!pageVisible || idle) setRequested(false); if (!pageVisible) setBudgetHit(false);`, with liveError/reconnects never reset, and `failed: liveError != null || budgetHit` keeps the tile off.
fix: In that effect, when !pageVisible also call `setLiveError(null); setReconnects(0);` so each visit gets one fresh attempt.

title: 'Show older' flips to a disabled 'Loading…' every minute during the background refresh
userImpact: Once a minute the button greys out and says 'Loading…' though nobody pressed it, and a tap in that moment is ignored.
evidence: refetchInterval: 60_000; `disabled={query.isFetching}` and `{query.isFetching ? 'Loading…' : `Show older (last ${RECORDING_DAY_STEPS[step + 1]} days)`}`.
fix: `const loadingOlder = query.isFetching && query.isPlaceholderData;` and use it for both `disabled` and the label.

title: A camera filter stays on after that camera's chip disappears, showing 'No recordings' with no chip selected
userImpact: If the filtered camera's last clip ages out during a refresh, the list goes empty ('No recordings in the last 7 days.') with no chip pressed, though other cameras have clips.
evidence: Chips are built only from loaded recordings (`for (const r of all) if (!seen.has(r.cameraId)) …`), `shown = cameraFilter ? all.filter(...) : all`, and cameraFilter is never reset.
fix: Add `useEffect(() => { if (cameraFilter && !cameras.some(([id]) => id === cameraFilter)) setCameraFilter(null); }, [cameras, cameraFilter]);` or always render a chip for the selected camera.

title: After 'Show older', the header says 'in the last 14 days' while still showing the 7-day list
userImpact: While the older recordings load, the count reads '43 in the last 14 days' (really 7 days), and an empty week reads 'No recordings in the last 14 days.'
evidence: `const days = RECORDING_DAY_STEPS[step];` changes immediately while `placeholderData: (prev) => prev` keeps the 7-day data; text is `{shown.length} in the last {days} days` / `No recordings in the last {days} days.`

title: On phones, recording thumbnails only start loading once they are on screen, so each one pops in late
userImpact: On iPhone each recording row scrolls in with a grey ▶ placeholder and its picture pops in a moment later, instead of being fetched just ahead of the scroll.
evidence: Playwright Chromium (scratch/b11/io.cjs), row 100 px below the fold, rootMargin '200px': window scrolling -> intersecting = true; page scrolling inside an overflow-y:auto box (like App.tsx data-page-scroller below lg) -> intersecting = false.

title: Recordings on desktop are one long column of full-width bars with tiny thumbnails
userImpact: Only ~5 clips fit above the fold, the page is 5,259px tall, and 85% of each row is empty space; the clip length is printed twice.
evidence: screenshot cameras-recordings-desktop-light.png: rows span 1,056px with a 144px thumbnail and '4:58 PM / Driveway · 0:24' at the left; thumbnail badge also says '0:24'. Code: <ul className="flex flex-col gap-2"> for every day group; duration in the badge (:63) and in the caption (:335).

title: Pressing → to skip ahead in a recording jumps to the next clip instead (desktop)
userImpact: On a computer, after clicking the video, pressing an arrow key to seek switches to the next or previous recording.
evidence: Playwright Chromium (scratch/b11/videokey.cjs): after clicking a <video controls>, activeElement = VIDEO and a window keydown listener receives 'ArrowRight target=VIDEO prevented=false', so Player's `else if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' && hasNewer) onStep('newer')` fires.
fix: In onKey, skip the arrow shortcuts when `e.defaultPrevented` or `(e.target as HTMLElement | null)?.closest('video, input, textarea, select')`; or move stepping to other keys (e.g. PageUp/PageDown or [ / ]).

title: 'Moving to Position 1…' stays under the camera long after it got there
userImpact: The 'Moving to …' message (with an ellipsis while live) stays for the rest of the visit, reading as if the camera is still moving.
evidence: `await goToCameraPreset(camera.id, index); setNote(watching ? `Moving to ${name}…` : `Moving to ${name}.`);` and nothing clears `note` except the next preset tap.
fix: After setNote, start a timer (ref, cleared on the next go() and on unmount) that clears the note after ~6 s, or switches it to `At ${name}.`.

title: Roomba Controls shows raw robot text ('clean_rooms · OK', 'dock · PENDING') and says a command was 'sent' while it is still queued
userImpact: The admin sees developer text in the Controls card and '"dock" sent' next to a chip that still reads 'dock · PENDING'; the footnote defines 'sent' as accepted by the robot, which matches neither.
evidence: onSuccess: ``setNote(`"${cmd.command}" sent — the robot may take a few seconds to respond.`)`` fires when the POST returns a row created with `.status("PENDING")` (RoombaService.java:256). Chip prints raw `{last.command} · {last.status}`; the poller marks 'SENT' when it claims the row and 'OK' when the broker accepted (poller.py:1376-1385, types/index.ts:339). Footnote: 'A “sent” command was accepted by the robot, not guaranteed to run'. Screenshot review: screenshot roomba-overview-desktop-dark-full.png: top-right of Controls reads 'clean_rooms · OK'. Code: {last.command} · {last.status}; the sent-note (:53) also echoes `"${cmd.command}" sent`.
fix: In RoombaControls.tsx map command names to words (clean_rooms -> 'Clean rooms', dock -> 'Send to dock', ...) and statuses to words (PENDING -> Queued, SENT -> Sending, OK -> Accepted, FAILED -> Failed), ideally with a time ('Clean rooms · accepted 2 min ago') at L71; change the success note (L53) to `"${label}" queued — the robot picks it up within a few seconds.`; reword the footnote (L96) to 'Accepted means the robot took the command, not that it ran — watch the status above.'

title: Room buttons on the Roomba map are probably not announced by screen readers
userImpact: A screen-reader user tabbing through the map may hear only 'Roomba floor plan' for every room instead of 'Rename Kitchen' / 'Clean Kitchen'.
evidence: `<svg ... role="img" aria-label={`Roomba floor plan...`}>` wraps the hit areas `<g className="roomba-roomhit..." role="button" tabIndex={0} aria-label={... `Rename ${roomLabel}`}>`. In WAI-ARIA the img role has 'Children Presentational: True', so descendants' roles and names are not supposed to be exposed (axe flags this pattern as nested-interactive).
fix: In RoombaMap.tsx use `role={interactive ? 'group' : 'img'}` on the svg (compute `interactive = canEdit || isMerging || isCleaning` beside the existing flags), keeping the aria-label.

title: Room labels on the Roomba map can sit off-centre or outside an L-shaped room
userImpact: A room with an L shape or unevenly spaced outline points may have its name drawn over a neighbouring room.
evidence: Label anchor is the plain average of the outer ring's vertices (lines 316-324), including the repeated closing vertex. Reproduction (scratch/b2.js): candidate's L-shaped hallway -> vertex mean (8.83, 5.63), point-in-ring false; 4x3 rectangle with closed ring -> (1.60, 1.20) vs true centre (2.00, 1.50), i.e. 20% of the way toward the first corner.
fix: In the rooms loop drop the duplicated closing vertex, compute the area-weighted (shoelace) centroid, and if `pointInRing(cx, cy, outerPts)` is false fall back to an interior point (e.g. midpoint of the widest horizontal span through the bounding-box centre, or a small pole-of-inaccessibility search).

title: Room names on the Roomba map are about 8px tall on a phone
userImpact: On an iPhone the room labels on the floor plan are tiny (around 8px, the pencil/broom icons about 6px), so the map is hard to read without squinting.
evidence: Font sizes are in viewBox units (`maxDim * 0.026`, prompt 0.022, glyph 0.02) and the long side is always 1000 + 2x60 = 1120 units. Reproduction (scratch/b2.js; SVG width on a 390px phone = 390 - 16 shell - 42 card - 26 map box = 306px): wide 14x9 plan -> name 8.0px, prompt 6.7px, glyph 6.1px; square plan -> same; tall 9x14 plan -> 11.7 / 9.9 / 9.0px; 430px phone, wide plan -> 9.0px; desktop (max-w-xl) -> 14.3px.
fix: In RoombaMap.tsx measure the rendered SVG width (ResizeObserver on svgRef) and compute label size as `Math.max(maxDim * 0.026, 12 * width / renderedPx)` so text never drops below ~12 CSS px (same for the prompt and glyph sizes, and scale the label stroke with it); or render labels as absolutely-positioned HTML over the SVG.

title: While dividing a room, pressing Enter on "Cancel divide" or "Undo corner" finishes the divide instead
userImpact: With two or more corners placed, tabbing to Cancel divide (or any other button on the page) and pressing Enter opens the divide confirmation instead of doing what the focused button says.
evidence: `window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)` while splitMode; `if (e.key === 'Enter' && n >= 2) { e.preventDefault(); onSplitFinish?.(); }` with no check of `e.target`. preventDefault on the Enter keydown suppresses the focused button's click, and `finishSplit` (Roomba.tsx:310-318) opens RoomSplitModal and clears the draft. Backspace is handled the same way but is harmless on buttons.
fix: At the top of onKey in RoombaMap.tsx return early when the event comes from a control: `const t = e.target as HTMLElement | null; if (t?.closest('button, a, input, select, textarea, [role="button"]')) return;` (or attach the shortcut to the map container and make it focusable).

title: "Recent incidents" on the Maintenance view appears to show all-time stuck/cliff/pickup totals
userImpact: A robot that has not been stuck in weeks would still show e.g. '23 stuck · 148 cliff · 61 pickup' under 'Recent', and the numbers would only ever grow.
evidence: `{wearSummary && <Detail label="Recent incidents" value={wearSummary} />}`; wearSummary prints `status.wear.nStuck / nCliffsF / nPicks` raw (373-381); the poller stores `wear = stats.get("bbrun")` from the ro-stats shadow with no windowing or differencing, next to `bbmssn.nMssn` (lifetime missions) and `bbsys` (lifetime hours) from the same payload.

title: Roomba shows raw robot codes: 'Mop pad fitted: padPlate' and 'Cycle: clean'
userImpact: Robot health reads 'MOP PAD FITTED padPlate' and a run's details read 'CYCLE clean' — internal values instead of words.

title: Roomba schedule card tells non-admins to click a button they don't have, and shows the same message when loading fails

[]` with no `query.isError` branch; the `refresh` mutation defines only onSuccess and the component never reads `refresh.isError`.

In RoombaNativeSchedules.tsx: empty text `isAdmin ? 'No schedules read yet — click "Refresh from robot"...' : 'No schedules set up yet.'`; add `query.isError ? "Couldn't load schedules — try again in a moment."` ahead of the empty branch; show `refresh.isError &&

` under the button.

title: "Lifetime Runs" can show 50 (the size of the history list) or "— missions" when the robot's lifetime counter is missing
userImpact: For a poll cycle the tile can drop from the real lifetime count (e.g. 188) to '50 missions', a number that is just how many history rows were fetched.
evidence: `: status?.lifetimeMissions != null ? String(status.lifetimeMissions) : String(totalRuns || '—')` with `unit={running ? '' : 'missions'}`; `totalRuns = runs.length`; runs come from `fetchRoombaRuns(50)`. node: `String(50 || '—') + ' missions'` -> "50 missions", `String(0 || '—') + ' missions'` -> "— missions". Poller: `stats = {}` when the ro-stats read throws (poller.py:954-958) -> `lifetime_missions = None` -> `lifetime_missions = EXCLUDED.lifetime_missions` overwrites the stored value with NULL.

Optionally in poller.py use `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.lifetime_missions, roomba_status.lifetime_missions)` (same for lifetime_run_minutes, charge_cycles, wear) so a failed stats read does not blank them.

title: The same number is called "Lifetime Time … hrs" on Overview and "Powered-on time … hr" on Maintenance
userImpact: 'Lifetime Time 319 hrs' reads like hours spent cleaning; it is the robot's powered-on counter, labelled correctly only on the other sub-tab.
evidence: Overview: `label="Lifetime Time" value={String(Math.round(status.lifetimeRunMinutes / 60))} unit="hrs"`. Maintenance: `<Detail label="Powered-on time" value={`${Math.round(status.lifetimeRunMinutes / 60)} hr`} />`. Source is `bbsys` hr/min (poller.py:235-237); roomba-v4-integration/enhancements/telemetry.md:30 states it 'is powered-on time'.

title: While the robot recharges mid-clean, the tiles switch to "Last Area" and "Lifetime Runs" as if the run were over
userImpact: The header says 'Recharging mid-clean · 604 sq ft cleaned so far' while the tile below labels the same 604 sq ft 'Last Area'.
evidence: Hero: `${(running || recharging) && status.sqft ? ` · ${status.sqft} sq ft cleaned so far` : ''}` with `recharging = isRecharging(status)` (phase 'charge' with a non-'none' cycle). Tiles: `label={running ? 'This Run' : 'Last Area'}` and `label={running ? 'Runtime' : 'Lifetime Runs'}` use `running` only, and running is false for phase 'charge' (backend RUNNING_PHASES = run, evac).

For the third tile keep 'Lifetime Runs' while recharging unless runtime is computed from `status.missionStart`, because the poller writes runtime_minutes = NULL for phase 'charge' (poller.py:223, 307).

title: Recent runs list stutters while scrolling and shows fewer rows than intended because rows are taller than the list assumes
userImpact: Scrolling the run history jerks upward by about 8 px (10 px on desktop) at every row once past the sixth run, and the box fits 7 rows (6 on desktop) instead of 8.
evidence: `height={Math.min(runs.length, 8) * 56 + 8}` / `itemHeight={56}`, but each row is `py-3` + a text-sm line + a text-2xs line + `border-b`. Built CSS (dist/assets/index-C53PHXy1.css): `.text-sm{font-size:var(--text-sm);line-height:var(--tw-leading,var(--text-sm--line-height))}`, `--text-sm--line-height:calc(1.25 / .875)`, `.text-2xs{font-size:var(--text-2xs)}` (inherits the 1.4286 ratio). scratch/b7.js: phone row = 63.57 px, desktop (>=1024) = 66.43 px vs 56. Simulating VirtualizedList (`offsetTop = start*itemHeight`): scrollTop 391 -> row 12 at y=371.9, scrollTop 392 -> y=363.3 (an 8.6 px move for 1 px of scroll), repeating at 448, 504, ...
fix: Make the row height explicit and equal to itemHeight: on the row `<button>` (line 827) add `h-[68px]` and drop `py-3` from the four cells (the grid already has `items-center`), then pass `itemHeight={68}` and `height={Math.min(runs.length, 8) * 68}`. 68 clears the 66.4 px desktop content; `h-16`/64 would clip on desktop.

title: Run history rows are announced only as "View details for the run on <date>", so same-day runs sound identical
userImpact: A screen-reader user cannot tell two runs on the same day apart and never hears the time, duration or outcome that sighted users see in the row.
evidence: `aria-label={`View details for the run on ${dateLabel}`}` on the row `<button>`; `dateLabel` is month/day/year only (803-809). An aria-label on a button replaces its content as the accessible name, hiding timeLabel, rooms, duration and status.
fix: Remove the aria-label so the row's own text is the name, or build it from the visible parts: `${dateLabel} ${timeLabel}, ${formatDuration(listDuration)}, ${st.label}. View details`.

title: A long Mission ID can run off the side of the run-details window on a phone
userImpact: If the robot's mission ID is a long unbroken string, it is cut off at the window's right edge and the window gains a sideways scroll.
evidence: Row value is `` in a `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-4` row next to a `shrink-0` label: a flex item defaults to min-width:auto, so it cannot shrink below its longest unbreakable word, and there is no `min-w-0`/`break-all`. On a 390px phone the content box is 390 - 32 (modal-overlay padding) - 2 (border) - 48 (p-6) = 308px; 'MISSION ID' + gap takes roughly 110px, leaving about 200px. `.modal-panel` sets overflow-y:auto, which makes overflow-x auto too. Screenshot review: screenshot overlay-roomba-run-detail-phone-dark.png: 'MISSION ID 01KA3D2P7M5QXT9B4N8RW6HZ(' runs past the panel padding and is clipped. Code: the Row value `{value}` (line 65) has no min-w-0 or break-all and sits next to a `shrink-0` label (line 64). It is used for run.missionId (line 154). Editor's spot-check: the screenshot used the audit's own fixture IDs (26-character ULIDs from scratchpad/gen/roomba-fixture-gen.js), not real data, and the repo redacts the real format, so the overflow is proven only for IDs of that shape. To confirm: SELECT mission_id FROM roomba_runs WHERE mission_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 3 on the NUC, or open a recent run on a phone.
fix: In Row add `min-w-0 break-all` (or `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]`) to the value span - harmless for the other rows - or drop Mission ID from this family-facing view.

title: Run details show "Ended" as a time with no date, so an overnight run looks like it ended before it started
userImpact: A clean that starts in the evening and finishes after midnight reads 'Started 6:40 PM / Ended 5:32 AM' under the start date with no hint it ended the next day; a run cancelled at once shows '0 min' in the list but '<1 min' in its details.
evidence: Reproduction (scratch/b2.js with the component's own formatters): `Mon, Oct 26, 2026 | Started 6:40 PM | Ended 5:32 AM`; `list vs dialog for 0 min: 0 min / <1 min`. Lines 130-131 use `fmtTime` (time only) for both rows; the title is `fmtDate(run.startedAt)` only. utils/roomba.ts notes 'a whole-house clean here is ~4 h of cleaning spread over ~11 h', so evening starts do cross midnight.
fix: In RoomRunDetailModal, when `completedAt` falls on a different calendar day than `startedAt`, render Ended as e.g. 'Tue, Oct 27 · 5:32 AM' (or append '(next day)'). Move one duration formatter into utils/roomba.ts and use it from both Roomba.tsx and the modal.

title: If the floor map has not loaded, Start a clean ignores the chosen Suction / Passes / Mode without saying so
userImpact: In the rare case the map request failed or is still loading, an admin can pick Max suction or Mop only, press Start, see "Cleaning started", and the robot runs its defaults.
evidence: mutationFn: roomIds.length === 0 ? sendRoombaCommand('start') : cleanRoombaRooms(roomIds, suction, passes, mode). The three selects are only disabled by submitting || done, and canStart is true for scope 'all' with zero rooms. rooms comes from mapQuery.data?.geojson?.rooms?.features ?? [] and the Clean button (Roomba.tsx:587) does not wait for the map.
fix: In CleanModal.tsx, when rooms.length === 0 disable the three selects and show a one-line hint under them ("Options need the floor map - this will run a standard clean"), so the documented fallback is visible. Keep the fallback itself.

title: Start a clean cannot be scrolled: with the phone sideways the Start button is off-screen, and on a small phone the room list squeezes to a sliver
userImpact: An admin holding the phone in landscape cannot reach Cancel / Start cleaning; on an iPhone SE-sized screen the room checklist can shrink to almost nothing.

Rendered with the built CSS in headless Chromium (scratch/b1-layout.mjs): 852x393 current -> panel 334px, content 447px, Start button bottom at 477px of a 393px viewport, overflow visible (not scrollable); same markup with modal-panel -> scrollable. 375x667, Pick rooms + status line: room list height collapses to 14px. Portrait 393x852: fine in both variants.

title: Start a clean shows the sentence "Cleaning 2 rooms selected." (and "Cleaning 0 rooms selected.")
userImpact: In Pick rooms mode the summary line under the room list reads as a broken sentence.
evidence: Line 184: Cleaning {selectLabel}. with selectLabel = `${n} room(s) selected` for the select scope. Reproduced (scratch/b1-misc.mjs): "Cleaning the whole house · 6 rooms." / "Cleaning 0 rooms selected." / "Cleaning 1 room selected." / "Cleaning 2 rooms selected."

title: If the robot's status goes stale mid-clean, the page shows "Offline" next to a pulsing LIVE badge and "Cleaning"
userImpact: After the poller loses the robot during a run, the header contradicts itself (Offline, updated hours ago, yet LIVE / Cleaning / a frozen Runtime) until the poller reconnects.
evidence: `const running = status?.running ?? false;` gates the LIVE pill (414), the 'Cleaning' chip (352) and 'This Run … cleaning now' (551-556) with no reference to `status.online`. Backend computes them independently: `running = RUNNING_PHASES.contains(phase)` from the last stored row, `online = updatedAt.isAfter(now - 10 min)` (RoombaService:696-699). The poller only rewrites the row (and `updated_at = NOW()`) on a successful cycle; a failed cycle logs 'Cycle failed … will reconnect' and leaves phase 'run' in place.
fix: Derive `const live = running && !!status?.online` and use it for the LIVE pill, the dockChip 'Cleaning' branch, the tile labels/subtitle and RoombaMap's `running` prop; when `running && !status.online` show 'Last seen cleaning' in the sentence instead.

title: Roomba header briefly reads "No data · updated never" with an amber dot while the status is still loading
userImpact: Opening the Roomba tab cold shows a warning-coloured 'No data · updated never' and the generic name 'Roomba' for the length of the first request, then flips to the real name and 'Online'.
evidence: `{status?.online ? 'Online' : status ? 'Offline' : 'No data'}`, dot `status?.online ? 'bg-emerald-400' : 'bg-amber-400'`, `· updated {formatRelative(status?.updatedAt)}` where `formatRelative(undefined)` returns 'never' (line 60). None of it checks `statusLoading`, although the stat tiles (546) and the 'Waiting for your Roomba's first check-in' note (501) do.

title: While the dock empties the bin, the Roomba page and Home say 'Cleaning' (the 'Emptying' labels can never appear)
userImpact: For the short time the dock is emptying the bin, the Roomba chip says 'Cleaning', the LIVE badge pulses and the area tile says 'cleaning now', while the sentence on the same page says 'Emptying bin'; Home says 'Cleaning / Cleaning now'. It lasts well under a minute per dock visit, so it is only seen if a refresh lands in that window.
evidence: `if (running) return { text: 'Cleaning', ... }` (352) is evaluated before `if (status.phase === 'evac') return { text: 'Docked · emptying', ... }` (366). Backend: `RUNNING_PHASES = Set.of("run", "evac")` and `running = RUNNING_PHASES.contains(phase.toLowerCase())` (RoombaService:55, 696-697), so phase 'evac' always arrives with running=true and line 366 is dead code. `phaseLabel` (line 32) returns 'Emptying bin' for the same status. Also (home-4): Reproduction (scratch/b5.js) with the backend rule `running = phase in {run, evac}` (RoombaService.java:55, 696): phase 'evac' -> state 'Cleaning', pill 'Cleaning'. The `rb.phase === 'evac' ? 'Emptying'` branch at line 112 is unreachable because `rb.running` is tested first. Roomba.tsx has the same dead branch at 366 (chip says 'Cleaning' at 352) while phaseLabel (line 32) says 'Emptying bin'. Editor's spot-check of the disagreement: home-4 doubted the robot ever reports phase 'evac', citing roomba-v4-integration/enhancements/control.md:52, but that line is about the untested 'evac' command, not the phase. The robot has an auto-empty dock (FINDINGS.md:75 cap.evac: 1) and its runs record bin evacuations (RoomRunDetailModal.tsx:145 'Bin emptied'), so the state occurs; the unreachable branches are certain from the code.
fix: Test for phase 'evac' before 'running' everywhere: in Roomba.tsx move the `status.phase === 'evac'` return (L366) above `if (running)` (L352) and use `const cleaning = running && status?.phase !== 'evac'` for the LIVE pill (L414) and the 'cleaning now' subtitle (L556); in HomeSummary.tsx test `rb.phase === 'evac'` before `rb.running` in roombaState (L106) and roombaDetail (L154, e.g. 'Emptying the bin'). The backend deliberately counts evac as running (BUILD_CONTRACT.md:59), so leave RoombaService alone.

title: On a computer, selecting text in the Add/Edit Maintenance form and letting go of the mouse outside the panel closes the form and loses everything typed
userImpact: Drag-selecting text in Notes (or any field) and releasing past the panel edge throws away a long half-filled form with no confirmation; a stray tap in the 16px gutter beside the form does the same on a phone.

title: On phones the three-across rows in the Maintenance form are too narrow: date boxes show 'mm/dc' and the Cost box sits higher than its neighbours

title: Tapping Add Record while a photo is still uploading saves the record without the photo

title: 'Copy network details' says 'Copied' without checking, and does nothing at all when the app is opened over plain http on the home network
userImpact: Opened at the NUC's LAN address (http://192.168.x.x) the Copy button silently does nothing; over https it always flips to 'Copied to clipboard' whether or not the copy went through.
evidence: WiFiPage.tsx:57-58 `navigator.clipboard.writeText(lines.join('\n')); setCopySuccess(true);` - not awaited, no catch, no check that `navigator.clipboard` exists. `navigator.clipboard` is secure-context only, so on http://<lan-ip> it is undefined and line 57 throws a TypeError before `setCopySuccess` runs. docs/wifi-integration.md:68 documents opening this very tab at `http://192.168.4.228/wifi`; nginx/default.conf listens on plain :80 with HTTPS only via Tailscale. The codebase already does it properly in GuestHome.tsx:552-558 (`try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) ; set success } catch { 'Clipboard blocked...' }`).
fix: Make handleCopyNetwork async and mirror GuestHome.copySnapshot: `try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text); setCopySuccess(true); } catch { setCopyFailed(true) }` and show 'Couldn't copy - press and hold the password to copy it' on failure (the optional-chained/undefined clipboard case lands in the same catch). title: In dark mode the guest Wi-Fi QR code is inverted (white squares on navy), which some guests' phone scanners may not read
userImpact: A guest whose phone camera does not decode inverted QR codes would get no 'Join Network' prompt when the host's screen is in dark mode, with nothing on the page hinting why.
evidence: WiFiPage.tsx:37-40 `const color = { dark: theme === 'dark' ? '#f8fafc' : '#0f172a', light: theme === 'dark' ? '#0f172a' : '#ffffff' };` passed to both QRCode.toDataURL calls, so in dark theme the modules are #f8fafc on #0f172a (contrast 17.06:1, but polarity reversed from the QR spec). The small code uses `margin: 2` (spec quiet zone is 4), though it sits on a `bg-appsurface` tile that is the same #0f172a in dark theme, which effectively extends the quiet zone. Screenshot review: screenshots wifi-phone-dark-full.png and overlay-wifi-qr-phone-dark.png: QR modules #f8fafc on #0f172a; the light theme renders dark modules on white. Code: `dark: theme === 'dark' ? '#f8fafc' : '#0f172a', light: theme === 'dark' ? '#0f172a' : '#ffffff'` (lines 37-40), used for both the card and the 800px enlarged code. No comment marks the inversion as intentional. Whether a given phone reads it depends on its scanner, hence PLAUSIBLE.
fix: Always generate the code dark-on-white regardless of theme: `color: { dark: '#0f172a', light: '#ffffff' }`, drop `theme` from the effect's dependency list, use `margin: 4` for the small code too, and give the tile a white background (`bg-white` instead of `bg-appsurface`) so the white plate looks deliberate on the dark card. The enlarged dialog already has a dark panel that a white plate sits well on.

title: In Alert types the "Alerts" and "Phone" captions sit 9px to the right of the switches they label

title: The colour swatches show no keyboard focus or selected state, and the guest photo button is read out as '?'
userImpact: Tabbing through the 32 colour swatches (Edit Profile and the guest sign-in page) gives no visible sign of which one is focused, in either theme, and a screen reader can't tell which colour is chosen; on the guest page the photo picker is announced as '? camera, button'.

The codebase already knows this: MaintenanceDashboard.tsx:553 has `e.target.value = ''; // allow re-picking the same file after a failure`. UserEditModal and GuestLogin.tsx:22 lack that line.

title: After tapping "Don't Allow", Phone alerts says "see the steps above" but shows no steps
userImpact: A member who declines the notification prompt is told to follow steps that are not on screen; the 'Turn on alerts' button stays and does nothing useful until they leave Profile and come back.
evidence: `const env = useMemo(currentEnv, []);` captures `Notification.permission` once at mount, so `pushSupport(env)` stays 'ok' after the prompt. `enablePush()` returns 'denied' -> `setNote('Notifications are blocked — see the steps above.')`, but the body is still the `support === 'ok'` branch (the button); the 'denied' instructions at lines 95-101 only render when `support === 'denied'`, i.e. after a remount.
fix: Hold the environment in state (`const [env, setEnv] = useState(currentEnv)`) and call `setEnv(currentEnv())` after `enablePush()` resolves (in the non-granted branch or in `finally`), so the card switches to the 'Notifications are blocked... Settings → Notifications → HomeOS' instructions; then the note can be dropped or kept as is.

title: Audit Logs says it tracks administrative actions and every sign-in, but only shows each person's last sign-in and never shows role changes or disabled accounts
userImpact: An admin reading 'Track user logins, account events, guest activity, and administrative actions' would expect to find who was disabled or had their role changed and a history of sign-ins, but the feed can never contain those.
evidence: Hero copy at AuditLogs.tsx:125 promises 'user logins ... and administrative actions'. useActivityLog (lines 33-79) only ever pushes four kinds of row: one `login` per user from `u.lastLoginAt` (line 37, so only the most recent sign-in), `register`/`approved`, `guest_connect`, `thermostat`. The `denied`, `disabled`, `role_change` and `guest_expire` entries in typeColors/typeLabels (lines 88-92, 100-104) are never produced. Line 81 `return { logs, loading: users.isLoading }` ignores the other two queries, so guest and thermostat rows pop in after the skeleton has gone, and a failed users request leaves a silently partial feed (or the line 153 'No activity recorded yet' message).
fix: Reword the hero at lines 125-126 to what is shown, e.g. 'Each person's latest sign-in, new accounts and approvals, guest check-ins, and every thermostat change...'; delete the unused `denied`/`disabled`/`role_change`/`guest_expire` entries (and from the LogEntry type union) unless real events are added; make loading `users.isLoading || sessions.isLoading || thermostats.isLoading`. The missing error message is handled under consistency-21.

title: In the light theme the calendar icon on the custom-range date fields is invisible (white on white) and the picker opens dark
userImpact: On a desktop browser in the light theme there is no visible calendar button on the Start/End date fields, and the pop-up calendar is dark against a light page.

title: Manual sync buttons say nothing when the request fails, and keep their tick after a success
userImpact: If Generate Alerts / Retrain Forecast errors (or the request times out), the button just returns to its plain label with no message; a button that once succeeded keeps showing a tick even after the date range is changed.
evidence: `{trigger.isPending ? "⏳ Triggering…" : trigger.isSuccess ? `✓ ${label}` : label}` — no isError branch, mutation has only onSuccess. Runtime: POST /admin/sync/alerts -> 500 left the button reading "🔔 Generate Alerts" with no failure text anywhere in the section; POST /admin/sync/forecast -> 200 left "✓ 📈 Retrain Forecast" in place.
fix: In SyncButton add an error state: label `⚠ ${label} failed` plus a small rose line with `errorMessage(trigger.error)` under the button row; clear success/error with `trigger.reset()` after ~4 s (or in an effect keyed on `body`).

title: Five table shortcuts in the Query Console fill in a query that always fails (ORDER BY a "timestamp" column the table does not have)
userImpact: Clicking the notifications, guest_sessions, roomba_runs, weather_observations or maintenance_records pill and pressing Run never returns rows.
evidence: timestampTables includes those five names -> `SELECT * FROM ${t.name} ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20`. schema.sql and the JPA entities only define a `timestamp` column on electric_usage, hourly_electric_usage, gas_usage and app_events (grep of model/: only EnergyUsage and AppEvent have a `timestamp` field); the others use observation_date / started_at / connected_at / created_at. Runtime: clicking the `notifications` pill set the textarea to "SELECT * FROM notifications ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20".
fix: Replace the Set with a map of table -> real time column ({ weather_observations: "observation_date", notifications: "created_at", guest_sessions: "connected_at", roomba_runs: "started_at", maintenance_records: "created_at", plus the four real `timestamp` tables }) and keep `ORDER BY 1 DESC` as the fallback.

title: An admin can change their own role or disable their own account from the Users list, and a role change saves the moment it is picked
userImpact: If the only admin picks User/Guest on their own row (no confirmation) or confirms Disable on themselves, admin access is gone immediately and can only be restored by editing the database.
evidence: UserManagement.tsx:399 `onChange={(e) => { onRoleChange(e.target.value); onRoleUpdate(user.id, e.target.value); }}` — no confirm, and the component only reads `const { isAdmin } = useAuth()` (l.58), never the signed-in user's id. UserService.updateUserRole (l.348-356) and disableUser (l.359-373) have no self / last-admin check. JwtAuthFilter l.92-105 takes the role from the database 'so a demotion applies immediately', so the very next /api/admin call is a 403 (or a 401 + sign-out after a self-disable).
fix: In UserManagement.tsx pass the signed-in id down (`const { isAdmin, user: me } = useAuth()`; `isSelf={u.id === me?.userId}`) and in UserCard hide/disable the role <select> and the Disable button when isSelf (show 'This is you'). Optionally wrap the role onChange in a window.confirm when the change is to or from ADMIN. Belt and braces: have UserService.updateUserRole/disableUser refuse when it would leave zero active admins.

` sits outside both `isAdmin &&` blocks (l.364, l.376). The Users tab is not guestHidden (App.tsx:195) and the route is only behind ProtectedRoute (main.tsx:124). title: The "Members" number on Users counts guests, pending sign-ups and disabled/expired accounts too
userImpact: The tile shows a bigger number than the people listed under "Household Members" right below it, and it keeps growing as old guest accounts expire but stay in the list.
evidence: l.157-158 `Members` / `{allUsers.data?.length ?? '...'}` versus l.125 `memberUsers = users.filter((u) => u.role !== 'GUEST')` under the 'Household Members' heading. The API (`UserService.getAllUsers`, l.299 `userRepo.findAll()`) returns every row regardless of role or status, and expired guests are only marked EXPIRED, never deleted (l.412-414), so they stay in the count.
fix: UserManagement.tsx:158 — count what the heading below means: `allUsers.data?.filter((u) => u.role !== 'GUEST' && u.status === 'ACTIVE').length ?? '...'`. If the total is still wanted, relabel the tile 'People' or add a second 'Guests' figure.

title: On Who's Home, Edit can open with out-of-date name/type/owner if the device was changed elsewhere while the page was open, and Save writes the old values back
userImpact: If a member links an already-labelled device from Profile -> This device while the admin has Who's Home open, the admin's Edit form still shows the previous owner and saving it silently undoes the member's link.
evidence: Form state is seeded once per mount: l.82-84 `useState(d.name ?? '')`, `useState<DeviceType | ''>(initialType)`, `useState(d.ownerUserId != null ? String(d.ownerUserId) : '')`; the Edit button is only `onClick={() => setEditing(true)}` (l.125) and `reset()` is called only from Cancel (l.165). Rows are keyed `key={d.id}` inside the same <ul> (l.255), so the 60-second refetch re-renders them without remounting. PresenceService.checkLink always does `d.setOwnerUserId(userId)` (l.217) and leaves an existing label/type alone, so a labelled device stays in the 'Labeled devices' list with a new owner.
fix: WhosHome.tsx:125 — `onClick={() => { reset(); setEditing(true); }}` so the form is re-seeded from the current `d` each time it opens (reset already reads the latest props).

title: One failed background refresh replaces the whole Who's Home / NUC Health page with an error line, even though the last good data is still in hand
area: Admin > Who's Home and NUC Health
userImpact: A brief network drop during a poll wipes the page (and any half-typed device label) until the next successful poll, up to a minute later; NUC Health loses its last readings exactly when the server is struggling.
evidence: Reproduced with the installed query-core 5.101.4 and the app's defaults (retry: 1) in scratch/b10/rq.mjs: `after failed poll: { status: 'error', isLoading: false, isError: true, hasData: true, isRefetchError: true }` -> `WhosHome guard \`query.isError || !data\` -> true (whole page replaced by error card)`; `after next good poll: { status: 'success', isError: false, hasData: true }`. WhosHome.tsx:204 `if (query.isError || !data) { return (<Card>...Couldn't load who's home...` and NucHealth.tsx:521 `if (health.isError || !health.data)` both return early, which unmounts every DeviceRow and its local form state (WhosHome.tsx:79-84).
fix: WhosHome.tsx:204 and NucHealth.tsx:521 — change the guard to `if (!data)` / `if (!health.data)` (keep the error text for that case), and when `isError && data` render the page as usual with a slim note above it, the way TabUsage.tsx:97-101 and Climate.tsx:145 do (e.g. "Couldn't refresh - showing the last reading").

title: The documented "npm run lint" command cannot run: ESLint is not installed and has no config (developer-only)

Two eslint-disable comments for react-hooks/exhaustive-deps remain in src.
